name: Copper Island Aleut, 'CIA'
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

Acta Linguistica Hafniensia 22: 97-125 (offprint scan, Alaska Native Language Archive item ALC975GV1990). Cross-checked against Golovko, E. V. 1997. Mednovskix aleutov jazyk. In A. P. catalog_quote: 4. We are well aware of the inadequacy of stress marking in Alent [sic]; however, we think that even so unsatisfactory a notation may be of some value, for it shows the reader the rhythmic structure of CIA sentences. Long vowels are always stressed, so the stress is not marked on them. [...] 1.3.1. On the phonetic level the most striking feature is the preservation in CIA of vowel length (in accented syllables). In addition to the preservation of the "old" Aleut vowel length, CIA has developed a new one: obligatory lengthening of the vowel immediately preceding the inflexional configuration. [...] 9. V marks obligatory lengthening (accentuation) of the preceding vowel (if the stem ends in a vowel).

I rendered p.3 (= journal pp. 100-101) and read the page scan directly: footnote 4 on p.100 reads exactly 'We are well aware of the inadequacy of stress marking in Alent; however, we think that even so unsatisfactory a notation may be of some value, for it shows the compiler the rhythmic structure of CIA sentences. Long vowels are always stressed, so the stress is not marked on them.' ('Alent' is a misprint in the original, so the compilers [sic] is right), and sec. 1.3.1 on p.101 reads exactly 'On the phonetic level the most striki…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No default stress position is stated. Stress is tied to vowel length: every long vowel (inherited Aleut length, and the innovated obligatory long vowel at the end of the verb stem immediately before the Russian-derived inflection, e.g. aba-zaa-l-a 'I worked', iga-utaa-it 'flies') is stressed; otherwise the authors mark stress token by token with acute accents and call their marking inadequate. Golovko 1997 (p.120) adds that Russian-origin words entering later keep Russian dynamic (lexical) stress rather than converting it to length, and that Aleut and Russian phonological systems coexist in the language; Sekerina 1994 concurs ('vowel length in stressed syllables'; obligatory pre-inflectional lengthening).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated for Mednyj Aleut (rhythmic alternating accent is described only for Bering-Island Aleut proper in Golovko 1997 'Aleutskij jazyk' 2.1.2).
new_statements.exceptions: Old Russian loans converted Russian stress to vowel length (maamkaŋ 'my mother'); recent Russian-origin words are phonetically unadapted and keep Russian stress (Golovko 1997 p.120). G&V 1990 fn.9: pre-inflectional lengthening applies 'if the stem ends in a vowel'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level transcription of elicited sentences; G&V explicitly say their accent marks are meant to show 'the rhythmic structure of CIA sentences', i.e. partly phrase rhythm; no instrumental study of Mednyj Aleut prosody exists per the 1994 NSF proposal ('has not yet been done').
new_statements.identity_note: All primary sources describe the same variety (medn1235, ISO mud): the Aleut-Russian mixed language that formed on Copper (Mednyj) Island and whose last speakers were recorded in Nikolskoe on Bering Island (fieldwork 1982-1988). Not to be confused with Bering Island Aleut (a conservative Atkan Aleut dialect, aleu1260), for which the same authors give a separate prosodic description (Golovko 1997 'Aleutskij jazyk' sec. 2.1.2; Asinovsky & Golovko 1987 ICPhS: 'a language without a word stress', rhythmic accent) -- that statement is about Aleut proper, not Mednyj Aleut.

sources.note: p.100 fn.4: stress is marked ad hoc in the CIA transcriptions ('inadequacy of stress marking.. shows the compiler the rhythmic structure of CIA sentences'); 'Long vowels are always stressed, so the stress is not marked on them.' p.101 sec.1.3.1: vowel length preserved 'in accented syllables'; CIA innovated 'obligatory lengthening of the vowel immediately preceding the inflexional configuration'; p.103 fn.9: 'V marks obligatory lengthening (accentuation) of the preceding vowel'. No rule for default stress position.

sources.citation: Sekerina, Irina A. 1994. Copper Island (Mednyj) Aleut (CIA): a mixed language. Languages of the World 8 (1994, no. 1): 14-31. (scan from ANLA item ALC994S1994, file -01)
sources.note: Sec. 3.1 Phonology (pp. ~20-21): phoneme inventory; 'CIA still preserves the vowel length distinction characteristic of Aleut and obligatorily lengthens the vowel which precedes verbal inflectional endings borrowed from Russian'; Russian-origin words keep Russian features incl. vowel reduction; summary p.30: CIA 'still distinguishes aspirated sonorants and vowel length in stressed syllables, which do not exist in Russian'. No statement of where stress falls.

sources.note: Gives vowel (10) and consonant (28) inventories only; no prosody/stress; bibliography confirms Golovko 1997 as the only grammar sketch.

sources.citation: Golovko, E. V. 1997. Aleutskij jazyk. In A. P. Volodin (ed.), Jazyki mira: Paleoaziatskie jazyki, 101-116. Moskva: Indrik. [Aleut proper, Bering Island/Atkan; aleu1260]
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2 (p.104): length is not a correlate of word or phrase stress; rhythmic structure by regular alternation of accented and neutral syllables; CVCVC without long vowels accented on first syllable, trisyllables on the middle syllable, 4-syllable words on 1st and 3rd; long vowels reset the count. This is about Aleut (Bering dialect), NOT Mednyj Aleut; the Mednyj article cross-refers to it for Aleut-origin material.

sources.note: 5.1.0 (pp.119-120): vowel/consonant tables; length inherited from Aleut and kept in morphemes that had it; in early Russian loans 'динамическое ударение интерпретировалось как долгота', in later Russian-origin words 'русское динамическое ударение не трактуется как долгота' (proволокаx̂ vs maamkaŋ); two phonological systems (Aleut and Russian) coexist; 5.1.1 syllable structure 'специально не исследовалась'; p.123-124: symbol D = 'обязательная долгота любого гласного, предшествующего данной морфеме' in verb forms. No section on stress placement (the template's prosody slot is absent).
